text: Open any public Git repo's idea graph read-only in the normal UI
description: Paste a Git URL (GitHub or any host) and browse that project's .bowman graph in the ordinary Aimparency UI, marked read-only: a visible 'read-only' hint, and every edit attempt answered with a warning instead of an editor (Felix 2026-10-15: no separate viewer). Purpose: a 30-second demo and an easy way to show and explore real graphs, which supports getting outside users. Honest limit: Aimparency is local-first, so the person viewing still runs Aimparency; a hosted public viewer would be a separate decision (SaaS was cancelled).

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Read-only must be enforced where data is written, not only hidden in the UI.
A plain git clone works for every host and needs no credentials for public repos.
Reusing the normal UI keeps one product and makes the demo show the real thing.
A one-click link is what makes the read-only view shareable.
Read-only edit attempts need a non-blocking way to say 'not possible'; a toast is that channel.
